newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Modest earthquake rocks Taiwan, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Modest earthquake rocks Taiwan, no damage reported.

text.p: A moderate earthquake rattled northeastern Taiwan on Tuesday, rocking the capital Taipei just as families were sitting down to supper. There were no immediate reports of injuries and damage, officials said.

The Central Weather Bureau said the quake's magnitude registered 6.0 on the Richter scale and put its epicentre at 80.5 km (50 miles) due east of northeastern Ilan county and 85.6 km (53 miles) beneath the earth's surface.
The quake, which rocked the island at 19.05 local time (1105 GMT), set buildings swaying in the capital Taipei and was felt in most parts of the island, officials said.
The earthquake's highest Richter magnitude on land was three, recorded in Ilan and eastern Hualien.
Earthquakes are relatively common in Taiwan and rarely cause severe damage.
Magnitude six earthquakes are capable of causing widespread damage in urban areas.
